title: Rabbit Guy’s Roots
text: “You’re getting plenty of gratitude from the people you saved, you know. Gaelion-san’s worked her way into the political scene rather nicely and started up as chief, pushing through reforms left and right.”

“Gaelion did this once before, so nano, Gaelion knows exactly where and how the bad stuff’s going on. That country follows a policy where they’ll fall in line to some degree as long as a strong dragon emperor shows off some strength as a symbol, so Gaelion just showed them some strength, nano.”
Guhhh… Rival, you wretch!
“Spear Hero, don’t glare, nano. Gaelion won’t lay a hand on Naofumi, so calm down, nano.”
“You can govern that fast?”

“Gaelion herself is a newcomer as far as approval ratings go, but originally Shieldfreeden was terrified of the reign of terror from Takt’s dragon and the Aotatsu-species leader Nelshen, so the authority of Gaelion and Bow Hero works pretty effectively, nano.”
Rival puffed out her chest like this was her best subject.
“Wyndia-chan looked kind of lonely, saying Gaelion-chan’s gone independent, you know?”
“Gaelion will take Big Sister along there eventually too, nano.”

“Progress is going about as well as can be expected, I’d say? I paid my respects over at Siltvelt too. Since Wolf’s there, they’ve been considerate about things on their end, and Lars-chan and the others have been helping out, so we’ve managed to avoid any troublesome factions butting in.”

It seemed Father was managing to navigate Siltvelt smoothly thanks to Wolf, indeed. Apparently the voice of Claw Hero carries more weight than the authority of the representative species, and at the same time, with Wolf acting as an effective shield, Father was able to move about freely.

“You know, Wolf’s all like ‘vof’ and ‘voffuppen’ normally, playing around, but in Siltvelt he puts on this sharp look and keeps watch over everyone. If he was like that all the time it’d be pretty cool.”
“That guy’s just spoiled, isn’t he.”
“No mistake there, nano.”

“Well, I’ll just chalk it up to the gap being cute. Still… I do hear some bad-mouthing about Wolf here and there. Stuff like ‘the coward who killed his brother to become Claw Hero’… He made a really unpleasant face about it, but I guess there are people everywhere who twist the truth to suit themselves even after learning the facts.”

Apparently it was Wolf’s brother who’d had his claws stolen and been killed by Takt. And Wolf himself, too terrified to flee, had been captured alive and subjected to modification through human experimentation, indeed. Normally you can’t see it well because of the fur and such, but when he takes his demi-human form, the traces remain—so you can imagine just from the scars alone how miserable it must have been.
“Is this the dimension where I get to work behind the scenes? I can do things even the benevolent Shield Hero-sama can’t manage, you know?”
“Itsuki… don’t look so pleased about it. This much isn’t going to be a big problem. We’ve got excellent people among our allies—well, I guess I should say subordinates.”

That’d be Elephant, indeed. Apparently Panda’s foster father also carries quite a bit of clout too. Having the right connections, as they say. On top of that, through Éclair, Father had managed to negotiate well enough with the Genmu-species that apparently he wasn’t having any trouble at all in Siltvelt.
“Father! Why won’t you let me help you out, I say!”
All I ever got was wave duty—he never took me along at all!
“Motoyasu-kun, aren’t you supposed to be under house arrest! Well… I suppose the Siltvelt side might be fine?”
“Well, why not? Anyway, Naofumi-san, there’s something I’d like to discuss with you.”
“Nano nano. New discovery, nano.”
Rival was warily scanning the surroundings, indeed.
“Rafumi being around might make things complicated, nano.”
“She’s not showing up. Well, she’s split off to help maintain public order in Melromarc, so I guess she’s not here right now?”
“What happened, I say?”
“You’re in the same category as Rafumi. I’d rather you didn’t come to Shieldfreeden either.”
Rabbit Guy took the opportunity to warn me off, indeed.
“Motoyasu-kun. That being the case, I will take you to Siltvelt, but stay a bit removed this time.”
Blast it, I say!
“Well, there are some things worth knowing even a little about, so you may listen in on just the progress report.”
“It’d be strange if you didn’t remember, but you’re saying nothing, so nano, this is partly a confirmation, nano.”
“Rival, Rabbit Guy, it is a humiliation to receive mercy from the likes of you, I say.”
“Now now, so, did something happen?”
“I suppose it has. It seems even I finally get an event of my own.”
“Theo, aren’t you looking a little pleased with yourself?”
Rabbit Guy was wearing some kind of confident expression, indeed. Now that I think of it, Rabbit Guy had been lamenting having no dramatic event like Crocodile Guy or Wolf.
“Well, Spear Hero, it wouldn’t be strange if you had some idea about this too, nano. It’s your own fault for forgetting, nano.”
“What? I say?”
Did something happen with Rabbit Guy?

“It’s still just a suspicion at this stage of things, but… apparently I seem to have come from Shieldfreeden. When Gaelion-san introduced me to some capable noble she knows, he… well, he called me his cousin.”
“Oh!? So you found a clue about Theo’s family? Now that you mention it, that envoy from Siltvelt did say Theo’s way of speaking was close to a Shieldfreeden dialect.”
Somehow Father seemed to have some idea about this too, indeed.
“Was there a noble like that, I say?”
The one I remembered was that corrupt bastard… that root-cause noble who pushed Rival’s cause, I say!
“Spear Hero… the one you remember, nano. That’s the noble who proposed dragon worship to Naofumi, nano.”
Rival said this in a small voice while quickly averting her eyes, indeed.
“That bastard, I saaaaaaay! How far does he intend to get involved!”
If that man hadn’t made his proposal, Father would never have been taken from us in the first place, indeed!
“W-wait, wait a second, my cousin’s going to end up in a terrible situation if you keep this up!?”
“Spear Hero, nano, he hasn’t done anything to the extent that you’d have a grudge like you do with Takt, nano.”
“Motoyasu-kun, let’s not hold misplaced grudges, okay? Yeah, you’re staying behind for sure.”
“Guhhh, I saaaaay! Just how far will that noble go, attacking me from a position of safety, I say!”

“It’s not even really an attack, and Gaelion won the fight in the end anyway, so let’s not talk about killing him, nano. He’s a capable guy who’ll tell you things straight just because you’re family, nano. Gaelion rates his abilities highly, nano.”
“It must be something, for Gaelion-chan to say that much… about his political abilities, I mean.”
It made me want to vomit, hearing Rival call someone capable, indeed.
“So? Sounds like he’s that person’s relative, but how does that work?”

“Apparently it happened back in that man’s parents’ generation… My father was a noble of Shieldfreeden, and my mother was a native of the country that existed before it was called Shieldfreeden—she’d been enslaved during the invasion and put to work—and I was born from that.”

The dragon-worship noble and Rabbit Guy belonged to different species, indeed. But apparently the noble who seemed to be Rabbit Guy’s father had laid hands on his mother, who was a slave, and a child was born from it, indeed. Natives… ah, right, when I toured that factory in Shieldfreeden, there’d been documents about conflicts with the local natives and such. Come to think of it, there’d been pictures of rabbit demi-humans in there too. So that must be the roots of this Rabbit Guy, then?
“Wow… the child of a noble and a slave, and on top of that a child born between an invader and a native—that’s a complicated birth.”

“Apparently there was some degree of romantic feeling involved, and I was given preferential treatment. That man remembered me well enough that he’d apparently taken care of the rabbit boy at the estate.”
“So then how’d you end up all the way in Melromarc, or rather, sold off at an age young enough that Theo doesn’t even remember it?”
“Apparently, right around when I’d grown up some and a hereditary disease manifested, my father happened to die of an epidemic around the same time, and the remaining family sold me off.”
“Sold you off instead of confining you somewhere… I guess that’s a cultural difference? They didn’t want bloodline issues and such leaking outside, huh.”

What a troublesome family matter, indeed. Nobles are the same wherever you go, indeed. Well, even in the world I originally came from, rich folks did similar things, indeed. I think there were pigs in families with distinctively colored hair and special abilities too, indeed.
